sections.counterpoint:
## The Counterpoint
Morningstar argues the IPO valuation already prices in aggressive AI-satellite growth that may not materialize on the stated timeline. The analysis questions whether Starlink’s current subscriber economics can scale fast enough to justify the $1.8 trillion entry point once public reporting begins. Resolution would come with the first earnings release and any updates on direct-to-cell adoption rates.  
Source: https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiAFBVV95cUxNN3h4dFZNend3SH
sections.deep_dive:
### The Engineering Angle
The IPO prospectus makes explicit that launch hardware still operates at a loss while Starlink already contributes the bulk of revenue and profit. That split reveals the real economic bet: every incremental improvement in Falcon reuse or Raptor production cost directly subsidizes the Starship program that has not yet reached full reuse. Public markets will now price those improvements quarter by quarter rather than through private-round rumors.
